statement: The multi-bit request and response bundles must never be sampled by a synchronizer; only one-bit control signals pass through synchronizers.

not_verified.note: Whether bundle bits pass through a synchronizer is a structural/CDC property (TEST-015).

statement: The source must hold the multi-bit request and response bundles stable for the whole handshake.
The destination must load the multi-bit bundle only after the associated control bit has arrived.

not_verified.note: Loading the bundle before the control bit arrives behaves the same in zero-delay simulation; it is a timing property (TEST-015/016).

statement: The timing of the bundle paths must be bounded by set_max_delay constraints (Section 17).
The bridge must always support APB4 write and read transfers across two asynchronous clocks (FEAT-001, REQ-FUNC-001 to REQ-FUNC-009).
The bridge must always transport wait states and error responses across the crossing (FEAT-002).
The bridge must provide the two-phase handshake when PARA_APBCDC_HS_TYPE is 0 (FEAT-003).
The bridge must provide the four-phase handshake when PARA_APBCDC_HS_TYPE is 1 (FEAT-004).
The bridge must support selectable synchronizer depth with PARA_APBCDC_CELL_TYPE 1 to 4; 0 is for simulation only (FEAT-005).
The bridge must provide APB5 wake-up signaling when PARA_APBCDC_APB5 is 1 (FEAT-006).
The bridge must provide the APB5 user signals when PARA_APBCDC_APB5 is 1 and the width is above 0 (FEAT-007).
The IP must always deliver an executable SDC with the crossing constraints (FEAT-008).
The RTL must comply with REF-003 baseline; conflicts are resolved by revising the requirement or choosing a compliant implementation, not by a local RTL exception.

The IP implements the AMBA APB Issue D completer role on the requester-side interface and requester role on the completer-side interface, with PSTRB, PPROT, PSLVERR always present and APB5 signals in the APB5 profile.
The bridge shall start exactly one completer-side APB transfer with the same PWRITE, PADDR, PPROT, PSTRB and, for a write, PWDATA as driven in the Setup phase.
In APB5 the completer-side transfer shall carry the same PAUSER and, for a write, the same PWUSER as the requester-side Setup phase.
The bridge shall return the completer-side PRDATA of a read and PSLVERR unchanged on the requester side, valid in the cycle where PREADY is high.
In APB5 the bridge shall return PRUSER of a read and PBUSER unchanged on the requester side, valid when PREADY is high.
Transfers shall be carried in start order, one completer-side transfer per requester-side transfer, with no loss and no duplicate.
No new completer-side transfer shall start before the response of the previous one has been delivered.
Requester-side PREADY shall be low from the Setup phase until the response is available.
Requester-side PREADY shall then be high for exactly one i_clk_mst cycle, in a cycle in which PSEL and PENABLE are high.
Requester-side PREADY shall be raised only after the completer-side PREADY was seen, so completer wait states extend the requester-side transfer.
The bridge shall wait without limit for the completer response, with no timeout.
Requester-side PSLVERR shall not be high outside the PREADY cycle.
Requester-side PSLVERR shall not be high unless the completer-side PSLVERR was high at the end of the transfer.
The bridge shall accept the Setup phase of a new requester-side transfer in the cycle following the PREADY cycle (back-to-back).
On the completer side the bridge shall drive PSEL high for the whole transfer.
PENABLE shall be low in the Setup cycle and high from the next cycle until the transfer completes.
The bridge shall keep PADDR, PPROT, PWRITE, PWDATA, PSTRB, PAUSER and PWUSER unchanged from the Setup phase until PREADY is seen high.
The bridge shall drive PSEL and PENABLE low when no transfer is in progress.
PPROT and PSTRB shall be forwarded unchanged.
The bridge does not check that PSTRB is low in a read; it forwards what the requester drove.
The IP shall expose exactly the ports of Section 6.2 of the configured revision.
Every output of both APB interfaces shall be a flip-flop output with no logic after it, so it is glitch-free.
Outputs that need not be valid shall hold a stable value (reset value zero).
PSLVERR shall be low when PREADY is low.
The request bit shall toggle once per transfer and the acknowledge bit shall toggle once per transfer (two-phase handshake).
The four-phase handshake shall sequence request high, acknowledge high, request low, acknowledge low.
The function seen on the two APB interfaces shall be the same for both handshake types.
The request bundle in the requester-side hold register shall not change from the request launch edge until the acknowledge was seen.
The response bundle in the completer-side hold register shall not change from the acknowledge launch edge until the next request was seen.
The request bit shall be launched at the same edge the request bundle is loaded, and the acknowledge bit at the same edge the response bundle is loaded.

not_verified.note: Same-edge launch of the internal bit and bundle; structural check TEST-015.

statement: There shall be no logic between a launch flip-flop and its synchronizer.

not_verified.note: No logic before the synchronizer; structural.

statement: The requester side shall raise PREADY only after the acknowledge returned to 0.
The IP shall be correct for any frequency ratio and phase of i_clk_mst and i_clk_slv, including equal frequency.
Only the five crossings (request, request bundle, acknowledge, response bundle, wake-up) shall exist between the clock domains.
Each control bit shall cross through a synchronizer and no bundle bit shall cross through one.
Synchronizer depth shall follow PARA_APBCDC_CELL_TYPE: 1 and 2 two stages, 3 three stages, 4 four stages.

not_verified.note: Stage count is structural. The interface latency effect for CELL_TYPE=4 is covered by CHK-030.

statement: The value 0 (no stage) is for simulation only and shall not be used in a netlist.
Both resets shall be active-low with asynchronous assertion.
Every flip-flop of the domain shall be at its reset value: payload registers 0, request 0, acknowledge 0, FSMs IDLE, PSEL, PENABLE, PREADY, PSLVERR, PWAKEUP 0.
The two resets shall be asserted together and each released synchronously to its domain clock, outside the IP.
A transfer in flight when a reset is asserted is lost.
Asserting only one reset is not supported.

not_verified.note: Integration restriction; the stimulus never asserts a single reset.

statement: o_apb_pwakeup shall be a flip-flop output that is high whenever the synchronized i_apb_pwakeup is high or a completer-side transfer is in progress.
o_apb_pwakeup shall be high no later than o_apb_psel.
PAUSER, PWUSER, PRUSER, PBUSER shall be transported with the same timing rules as the other request and response fields; a signal with width parameter 0 is not present.
The APB5 signals shall have no effect: o_apb_pwakeup is 0 and user outputs are 0.
The IP shall accept the parameter values of Section 8.

not_verified.note: Elaboration of legal parameter values is a parameter sweep. Individual configurations are simulated in CHK-019, CHK-022 and CHK-030.

statement: Duration from first Setup cycle to end of the requester PREADY cycle shall not exceed (N+3) x T_mst + (N+3+w) x T_slv.
Duration from first Setup cycle to end of the requester PREADY cycle shall not exceed (2N+4) x T_mst + (2N+4+w) x T_slv.
The bridge shall carry one transfer at a time.
The IP shall be delivered with a Synopsys-dialect SDC defining the two clocks, interface budgets and exceptions of the five crossings, with budgets computed from clock periods and synchronizer depth.
Each crossing path shall be constrained by set_max_delay with clock latency ignored.
No set_clock_groups -asynchronous and no set_false_path, other than the hold-only false path of the crossings, shall exist between the two clocks.
The clock latency difference between launch and capture flip-flops of every crossing shall be smaller than the one-destination-period guard band.
The RTL shall comply with REF-003 and use the hierarchy of Section 14.2.

Synchronizer cells shall be instantiated only inside wrapper m_vlsit_apbcdc_cell_sync, named u_dont_touch_ followed by the function, with a simulation model adding random extra output latency of 0, 1 or 2 destination cycles.

not_verified.note: Wrapper naming and simulation model of the synchronizer cells. The model's extra latency is accounted for in the windows of the tests.

statement: Every waveform of the Section 10.3 plan shall exist as an image with its WaveJSON source, and the prototype scripts shall reproduce them.

The random regression shall cover both handshake types, two synchronizer depths, APB4 and APB5, at least ten clock ratios including equal and 9:1 both directions, with wait states and errors, and report no error.

not_verified.note: Regression composition across configurations and ratios; realized by running CHK-029 in multiple configurations, not a single simulation.

statement: CFG-MIN must be based on CFG-APB4 with FEAT-004, FEAT-006 and FEAT-007 disabled, ADDR_W 1 and DATA_W 8, as the smallest legal instance verified by TEST-014.
FEAT-004, FEAT-006 and FEAT-007 must be selected by an elaboration-time parameter and be present or absent, not enabled or disabled at run time.

not_verified.note: Features selected at elaboration; there is no run-time control port.

statement: With the two-phase handshake reg_req toggles; with the four-phase handshake reg_req rises.
Loading reg_req_payload and launching the request happen at the same clock edge.
The slv FSM loads reg_apb_payload from reg_req_payload, which has been stable for at least N destination periods, then raises PSEL (Setup).
PENABLE (Access) is raised one cycle after PSEL.
The slv FSM waits in ACCESS until the completer drives PREADY.
At that edge the slv block loads reg_resp_hold with PRDATA, PSLVERR, PRUSER, PBUSER, drops PSEL and PENABLE, and launches the acknowledge (toggle or rise).
The mst FSM loads the response output registers from reg_resp_hold and raises PREADY for one cycle (state RESP).
The mst FSM first drops the request, waits for the acknowledge to fall, then loads the response and raises PREADY.
The slv FSM waits in REQ0 for the request to fall and then drops the acknowledge.
The mst FSM returns to IDLE and captures the next Setup phase driven in the cycle after the PREADY cycle.
i_apb_pwakeup is registered in the mst block, crosses through u_sync_wk, and drives o_apb_pwakeup through a flip-flop in the slv block together with an in-progress term.
At most one transfer is in flight, and the FSMs are in IDLE only between transfers.
The request and response bundles change only while the handshake is not in the phase in which the other domain may load them.
With the two-phase handshake the request and acknowledge bits are equal; with the four-phase handshake both are 0.
Requester-side PREADY is high only in state RESP, for one cycle per transfer.
Completer-side PSEL is high only in states SETUP and ACCESS.
Every flip-flop that drives an APB output is reset to 0.
The IP provides interface IF-001, an AMBA APB4/APB5 Issue D completer interface (requests in, responses out) in CLK-MST, in all configurations.
The IP provides interface IF-002, an AMBA APB4/APB5 Issue D requester interface (requests out, responses in) in CLK-SLV, in all configurations.
The IP provides interface IF-003 as receiver of clocks and hardware resets (inputs) for CLK-MST and CLK-SLV, in all configurations.
o_apb_pslverr is a flop output that is high only in the o_apb_pready cycle, loaded with o_apb_pready and cleared at the next edge; reset value 0.
o_apb_pwrite is loaded with the request and stays stable until the transfer completes; reset value 0.
o_apb_paddr is loaded with the request and stays stable until the transfer completes; reset value 0.
o_apb_pprot is loaded with the request and stays stable until the transfer completes; reset value 0.
o_apb_pstrb is loaded with the request and stays stable until the transfer completes; reset value 0.
o_apb_pwdata is loaded with the request and stays stable until the transfer completes; reset value 0.
o_apb_pauser is loaded with the request and stays stable until the transfer completes; reset value 0.
o_apb_pwuser is loaded with the request and stays stable until the transfer completes; reset value 0.
A transfer starts with a one-cycle Setup phase (PSEL high, PENABLE low), followed by the Access phase (PENABLE high), which ends in the cycle where PREADY is high.
After PREADY the bus may return to IDLE or go directly to the Setup phase of the next transfer.
PADDR, PPROT, PENABLE, PWRITE, PAUSER, PSTRB, active PWDATA lanes and PWUSER of a write are valid whenever PSEL is high; the bridge captures them in the Setup cycle.
PREADY is valid when PSEL and PENABLE are high.
PRDATA of a read, PSLVERR, PRUSER of a read and PBUSER are valid when PSEL, PENABLE and PREADY are high.
PADDR, PPROT, PWRITE, PWDATA, PSTRB, PAUSER and PWUSER must not change between Setup and Access phase and while PREADY is low.
The bridge guarantees stability of the completer-side fields by loading them into reg_apb_payload once, relying on requester stability only in the Setup cycle.
PSLVERR is valid only in the last cycle of a transfer.
The bridge forwards PRDATA and PSLVERR together without masking, even for a read with an error.
PSTRB must be low in a read.
The bridge forwards PSTRB as received.
PWAKEUP must be glitch-free to be sampled asynchronously and must stay high until PREADY when high in the same cycle as PSEL.
PWAKEUP may be asserted before, during or after PSEL.
PWAKEUP should be asserted one cycle before PSEL.
A completer may wait for PWAKEUP before driving PREADY.
PAUSER and PWUSER are valid with PSEL (PWUSER also with PWRITE) and keep their value through Setup and Access phases.
PRUSER and PBUSER are valid in the PREADY cycle.
A domain-crossing bridge should provide all user signals.

not_verified.note: Should provide all user signals; the port list is fixed by DEC-021.

statement: The bridge performs one completer-side transfer and returns the response.
Requester-side PREADY stays low until the completer response.
The bridge returns PSLVERR with PREADY and forwards the data.
The bridge accepts a back-to-back transfer whose Setup phase follows right after PREADY.
The bridge ignores PENABLE high without a preceding Setup cycle and starts no transfer.
The bridge does not detect the change and uses the values captured in the Setup phase.
The bridge waits without limit for the completer PREADY.
A single reset asserted alone is not supported; both resets must be asserted together, and a transfer in flight is lost on reset.
The IP has no interrupt or event output; errors travel as PSLVERR of the transfer.
Only the five listed crossings (CDC-001 to CDC-005) join the CLK-MST and CLK-SLV domains; no other path exists between them.
Each data bundle must be held stable and loaded by the destination only after its control bit arrives, so no bundle bit passes through a synchronizer.

The request bundle reg_req_payload must be held in mst, loaded at the launch edge of the request bit, and loaded into reg_apb_payload in slv at the edge that sees the request event, without a synchronizer.
The request hold register reg_req_payload and reg_apb_payload must reset to 0.
reg_req must cross to slv through N-stage synchronizer u_sync_req with no logic between the flop and the first stage, its stages reset to 0 by i_rst_n_slv.

not_verified.note: Synchronizer structure. A consistent reset is functionally covered by CHK-027.

statement: reg_ack must cross to mst through N-stage synchronizer u_sync_ack with no logic before the first stage, reset to 0 by i_rst_n_mst.

not_verified.note: Synchronizer structure. Functionally covered by CHK-027.

statement: reg_resp_hold must be held in slv, loaded at the launch edge of the acknowledge bit, and loaded into reg_resp_payload in mst at the edge that sees the acknowledge event, without a synchronizer.
reg_resp_hold and reg_resp_payload must reset to 0.
reg_wakeup, a registered copy of i_apb_pwakeup, must cross to slv through N-stage synchronizer u_sync_wk, reset to 0 by i_rst_n_slv.
Release of one reset while the other domain is still in reset is allowed; no request is launched or seen because the mst FSM leaves IDLE only on a Setup phase.
On i_rst_n_mst assertion (active-low, asynchronous), all mst-block state resets: registers 0, FSM IDLE, o_apb_pready and o_apb_pslverr 0.
On i_rst_n_slv assertion (active-low, asynchronous), all slv-block state resets: registers 0, FSM IDLE, including o_apb_psel, o_apb_penable and o_apb_pwakeup.
No transfer may start before both resets are released; the requester keeps i_apb_psel low until then.
PARA_APBCDC_ADDR_W, default 32 and legal range 1 to 32, sets the width of PADDR and of the request bundle.
PARA_APBCDC_DATA_W, default 32 and legal values 8, 16 or 32, sets the width of PWDATA and PRDATA; PSTRB has DATA_W/8 bits.
PARA_APBCDC_APB5 selects APB4 (0, default) or APB5 (1); APB5 adds PWAKEUP and the user signals, and user widths apply only when 1.
PARA_APBCDC_USER_REQ_W (0 to 128, default 0) sets the width of PAUSER, only with PARA_APBCDC_APB5 = 1; 0 means no PAUSER.
PARA_APBCDC_USER_DATA_W (0 to DATA_W, default 0) sets the width of PWUSER and PRUSER, only with APB5 = 1; 0 means none.
PARA_APBCDC_USER_RESP_W (0 to 16, default 0) sets the width of PBUSER, only with PARA_APBCDC_APB5 = 1; 0 means no PBUSER.
PARA_APBCDC_HS_TYPE selects two-phase toggle (0, default) or four-phase level (1) handshake; latency and crossing events differ but APB interface function is the same.
PARA_APBCDC_CELL_TYPE (0 to 4, default 2) selects the synchronizer cell option, with N = 2, 2, 3, 4 stages for values 1 to 4.
Value 0 (bypass) is for simulation only and is rejected by the SDC.
LPARA_STRB_W is derived as DATA_W / 8, giving 1, 2 or 4.
LPARA_REQ_W equals ADDR_W + 3 + 1 + STRB_W + DATA_W, plus USER_REQ_W and USER_DATA_W in APB5, and is at least 7.

not_verified.note: Internal width LPARA_REQ_W; no check per designer decision.

statement: LPARA_RESP_W equals DATA_W + 1, plus USER_DATA_W and USER_RESP_W in APB5, and is at least 9.

not_verified.note: Internal width LPARA_RESP_W; no check per designer decision.

statement: Illegal configurations (bad data/address width, user width over limit or with APB5 = 0, out-of-range options) must not be used; the IP does not check them and behavior is unspecified.

not_verified.note: Illegal configurations are not used; behavior is unspecified.

statement: The bridge must move the fields unchanged and perform no arithmetic on them.
The address is a byte address of width PARA_APBCDC_ADDR_W and is forwarded without extension or truncation.
The data word of width PARA_APBCDC_DATA_W is opaque and is forwarded without extension or truncation.
Write strobes have width LPARA_STRB_W, one bit per byte lane (bit n for PWDATA bits 8n+7 to 8n), and are forwarded as received without extension or truncation.
Protection is 3 bits wide, encoded as APB (bit 0 privileged, bit 1 non-secure, bit 2 instruction), and forwarded as received.
The request bundle of width LPARA_REQ_W packs fields from the least significant bit in order PADDR, PPROT, PWRITE, PSTRB, PWDATA, PAUSER, PWUSER; a zero-width field contributes no bit.

not_verified.note: Internal bundle bit order. End-to-end field equality is checked by CHK-031 and CHK-029.

statement: The response bundle of width LPARA_RESP_W packs fields from the least significant bit in order PRDATA, PSLVERR, PRUSER, PBUSER; a zero-width field contributes no bit.

not_verified.note: Internal bundle bit order. Response equality is checked by CHK-033 and CHK-029.

statement: Request and acknowledge bits are 1 bit wide; in two-phase mode the value toggles per transfer and the request and acknowledge are equal when idle.
In four-phase mode the request and acknowledge bit is 1 while a phase is requested and 0 when idle.
The requester FSM must leave IDLE to WAIT, loading reg_req_payload and toggling reg_req (two-phase) or setting it (four-phase) at the exit edge.
In WAIT the requester must keep o_apb_pready low; on the acknowledge event it goes to RESP (two-phase, raising o_apb_pready) or clears reg_req and goes to CLOSE (four-phase).
In CLOSE reg_req must be 0; when the synchronized acknowledge falls the FSM loads the response registers, raises o_apb_pready and goes to RESP.
In RESP o_apb_pready must be high for one cycle, then the FSM returns to IDLE and clears o_apb_pready and o_apb_pslverr at the exit edge.
The completer FSM must go to SETUP, loading reg_apb_payload from the request bundle and driving o_apb_psel high at the exit edge.
In SETUP o_apb_penable must be low; the FSM always moves to ACCESS and sets o_apb_penable high at the exit edge.
On i_apb_pready high the FSM must load reg_resp_hold, drop o_apb_psel and o_apb_penable, toggle (two-phase) or set (four-phase) reg_ack, and go to IDLE (two-phase) or REQ0 (four-phase).
In REQ0 the FSM must wait for the synchronized request to fall, then clear reg_ack and go to IDLE.
The bridge must capture the fields, cross the request, run one APB write on the completer side and return the response, with PREADY for one cycle.
For a read the bridge must return PRDATA and PRUSER to the requester with PREADY.
The completer-side Access phase must last w + 1 cycles and requester-side PREADY must follow after the response.
PSLVERR must be carried in the response bundle and be high in the requester-side PREADY cycle.
The mst FSM must be back in IDLE and capture the Setup phase immediately, starting the second transfer at once; one transfer at a time.
o_apb_pwakeup must follow the synchronized wake-up OR the in-progress term and be high before or with o_apb_psel.
PAUSER and PWUSER must cross in the request bundle and PRUSER and PBUSER in the response bundle, with identical values on the other side.
State of the domain must clear asynchronously, all registers at reset value, and a transfer in flight is lost.
The bridge must use the four-phase handshake and give the same results as OP-001 and OP-002.
The slv FSM must see the event at edge N+1 of i_clk_slv, load reg_apb_payload, raise o_apb_psel, then pass SETUP and ACCESS, with o_apb_penable high from the second edge.
At the i_apb_pready edge the response must be held, acknowledge launched, and o_apb_psel and o_apb_penable low.
The mst FSM must load the response and raise o_apb_pready for one cycle, then go to IDLE.
A new Setup phase must not be driven by the requester before PREADY, since APB is non-pipelined.
Duration D from first Setup cycle to end of PREADY cycle must not exceed (N+3)xT_mst + (N+3+w)xT_slv; for equal clocks 2N+6+w cycles.
Duration D from first Setup cycle to end of PREADY cycle must not exceed (2N+4)xT_mst + (2N+4+w)xT_slv; for equal clocks 4N+8+w cycles.
Throughput is one transfer per duration D, with no pipelining of transfers.
The bridge must forward the completer PSLVERR so that o_apb_pslverr is high in the o_apb_pready cycle.
The next transfer must be independent of a previous transfer that completed with an error.
The bridge must wait without limit for PREADY, and the requester sees PREADY low during the wait.
The in-flight transfer must be lost and all state cleared; both resets must be released and the transfer restarted.
The bridge must use the values of the Setup cycle and must ignore PENABLE without a Setup; the violation is not detected.
The bridge must have no sticky error, no error counter and no error output other than PSLVERR.
Two-phase transfer duration must be at most (N + 3) x T_mst + (N + 3 + w) x T_slv.
Four-phase transfer duration must be at most (2N + 4) x T_mst + (2N + 4 + w) x T_slv.
Only one transfer is in flight, and the next Setup phase is accepted in the cycle after PREADY.
The RTL must follow the VLSIT RTL Design Rules v2 (REF-003) as the mandatory coding authority.
The RTL must comply with REF-003 except for the single deviation DEC-021 (PRT-03).
RTL must use one module per file with file name equal to module name, a structural top, ANSI ports with input wire and output logic, and reg_, w_, p_ff_, p_com_ naming.
Every flip-flop must have an asynchronous reset to 0.
SVA, testbench or prototype code must not be in the synthesis file list.
The register and instance names used by the SDC must be kept as named in the RTL.
There must be no register logic and no protocol adapter other than the two FSMs.
o_req must be a flop output launched at the Setup edge, resetting to 0, toggling per transfer in two-phase and high during the request phase in four-phase.

not_verified.note: Sub-block port o_req. Its function is covered end to end by CHK-031 and CHK-029.

statement: i_req_payload must be valid and stable when the request event is seen and loaded in CLK-SLV at that edge.

not_verified.note: Sub-block input. Request integrity is checked by CHK-029.

o_resp_payload must be the hold register loaded at the edge that sees i_apb_pready, reset 0, valid and stable.

Pin and cell names of library cells may keep the library style and are exempt from the naming rule.
Metastability behaviour, reset in the middle of random traffic and the APB protocol assertions shall be verified on the RTL.
Every third configuration uses a requester changing fields in the Access phase to check Setup values are used, and every third APB5 configuration uses a requester never driving PWAKEUP.
All 12 RTL waveforms must match the figure WaveJSON, internal rows included, and assertions must pass in the metastability branch for each scenario.
The fault of the completer side loading its request register every cycle instead of at the request event must be shown by the structural check (TEST-015) and the SDC (TEST-016).

statement: Elaboration, lint and simulation must pass for the legal parameter extremes.

not_verified.note: Elaboration/lint of the parameter extremes is a sweep.

statement: When o_apb_pready is high, i_apb_psel and i_apb_penable must be high (SVA-001, never fails).
o_apb_pready must be high for exactly one cycle per transfer (SVA-002).
o_apb_pslverr high must imply o_apb_pready high (SVA-003).
The requester-side response must equal the completer-side response of the same transfer (SVA-004, checked by scoreboard).
o_apb_penable must rise one cycle after o_apb_psel, and o_apb_penable high must imply o_apb_psel high (SVA-005).
Completer-side fields must not change while o_apb_psel is high and i_apb_pready is low (SVA-006).
o_apb_psel and o_apb_penable must be low when no transfer is in progress and in reset (SVA-007).
Completer-side fields must equal the values of the requester-side Setup cycle (SVA-008, checked by scoreboard).
The number of completer-side transfers must equal the number of requester-side transfers (SVA-009, scoreboard).
No second completer-side Setup phase may occur before o_apb_pready of the previous transfer (SVA-010).
The request hold register must be stable from request launch until acknowledge is seen, and the response hold register stable from acknowledge launch until the next request is seen (SVA-011).
In two-phase handshake the request bit must change exactly once and the acknowledge bit exactly once per transfer (SVA-012).
In four-phase handshake the sequence must be request high, acknowledge high, request low, acknowledge low, then o_apb_pready (SVA-013).
o_apb_pwakeup must be high no later than o_apb_psel (SVA-014).
o_apb_pwakeup must stay high until i_apb_pready when it is high with o_apb_psel (SVA-015).
In reset every output must be at its reset value (SVA-016).
After reset no output may be unknown; o_apb_prdata must not be unknown when o_apb_pready of a read is high (SVA-017).
The duration of every transfer must be within the bound of REQ-PERF-001 or REQ-PERF-002 (SVA-018).

A CDC tool or the structural check of TEST-015 must confirm only control bits pass through synchronizers, no logic precedes a first stage, and no other path joins the domains across the five crossings.
The RTL shall contain no latch, no combinational loop, no tri-state, no clock gating and no derived clock, so that scan insertion is possible.
The IP shall have no DFT ports; a test reset override belongs to the SoC wrapper or reset controller.
EXC-001 shall constrain reg_req_payload to reg_apb_payload with set_max_delay -ignore_clock_latency of (N - 1) x T_slv and set_false_path -hold, hold not checked.
EXC-002 shall constrain reg_req to u_sync_req cells with maximum delay T_slv, ignoring clock latency, and hold not checked.
EXC-003 shall constrain reg_ack to u_sync_ack cells with maximum delay T_mst, ignoring clock latency, and hold not checked.
EXC-004 shall constrain reg_resp_hold (slv) to reg_resp_payload (mst) with maximum delay (N - 1) x T_mst, ignoring clock latency, hold not checked.
EXC-005 shall constrain reg_wakeup to u_sync_wk cells with maximum delay T_slv, ignoring clock latency, and hold not checked.
Required max transition, max capacitance and max fanout shall follow the project defaults.
The SDC shall not use set_clock_groups -asynchronous, set_false_path, or set_max_delay without the latency option between clk_mst and clk_slv.
The bundle shall be stable at the destination flop before the control bit, having crossed N synchronizer stages, tells the destination FSM to load it.

statement: The post-CTS clock latency difference shall stay below the one destination period guard band (REQ-TIM-003).
Each launch flop of a crossing control bit and its first synchronizer stage shall be placed adjacent.

not_verified.note: Placement; per designer decision, not verifiable in this flow.

statement: The two bundle registers of each direction should be placed close to each other.
The clock controller of the slv domain shall act on i_apb_pwakeup (or on a requester signal) before the request arrives, since the bridge cannot see requests while the clock is stopped.
The APB requester must issue one Setup phase then Access until PREADY, keep fields stable, and keep PSTRB low in a read.
The clock controller using PWAKEUP must keep i_clk_slv running while a request is in flight, since the bridge cannot detect a request on a stopped clock.

not_verified.note: Clock controller assumption; clocks run free in simulation.

statement: One parameter selects APB4 or APB5; APB5 adds PWAKEUP and user signals with configurable widths; no parity check signals are provided.
ADDR_W defaults to 32 (range 1 to 32), DATA_W defaults to 32 (8, 16 or 32), PSTRB and PPROT are always present, and user widths default to 0.
Every APB output must be a flip-flop output; PREADY must be high only in state RESP, i.e. only once the Access phase has been reached.
The response must be delivered only after the handshake has closed (acknowledge low), so the next Setup phase can always be accepted.
The RTL top must declare the APB5 ports in every configuration, with user widths of at least 1, unused inputs ignored and unused outputs 0.
Multi-bit bundled data must be held stable while the one-bit control signal crosses the domains.
The destination must load the bundled multi-bit data only after the control signal has arrived.

not_verified.note: Load-after-arrival is equivalent in zero-delay simulation; it is a timing property.
